ENGLISH — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #12
====

GRADE: Grade 7
SUBJECT: ENGLISH
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KJSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. A noun is a word that names: (1 mark)
   A. Only a describing word
   B. A person, place, thing, or idea
   C. Only an action
   D. Only a joining word

2. The past tense of “go” is: (1 mark)
   A. went
   B. goed
   C. going
   D. goes

3. When practising Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Conversational Skills: Polite Language, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Conversational Skills: Polite Language.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Conversational Skills: Polite Language.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Conversational Skills: Polite Language.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Conversational Skills: Polite Language.

4. When practising Reading 2.4.1 Intensive Reading: Class Reader, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 2.4.1 Intensive Reading: Class Reader.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Reading 2.4.1 Intensive Reading: Class Reader.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 2.4.1 Intensive Reading: Class Reader.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Reading 2.4.1 Intensive Reading: Class Reader.

5. When practising Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns.

6. Which word is a verb? (1 mark)
   A. run
   B. blue
   C. quickly
   D. happiness

7. Choose the correctly punctuated sentence. (1 mark)
   A. Where is the library
   B. Where is the library?
   C. Where is the Library
   D. where is the library

8. When practising Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Presentations: Oral Narratives, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Presentations: Oral Narratives.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Presentations: Oral Narratives.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Presentations: Oral Narratives.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Presentations: Oral Narratives.

9. When practising Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading: Independent Reading, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading: Independent Reading.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading: Independent Reading.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading: Independent Reading.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading: Independent Reading.

10. When practising Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns.

11. When practising Reading 2.2.1 Intensive reading: Simple poems, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Reading 2.2.1 Intensive reading: Simple poems.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Reading 2.2.1 Intensive reading: Simple poems.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 2.2.1 Intensive reading: Simple poems.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 2.2.1 Intensive reading: Simple poems.

12. A paragraph should usually have: (1 mark)
   A. Many unrelated topics with no link
   B. Only one word repeated
   C. No full stops
   D. One main idea with supporting sentences

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Listening and Speaking 15.1.1 Oral Reports and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Oral Reports and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Reading 15.2.1 Reading Fluency and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Grammar in Use 15.3.1 Affirmative and Negative Sentences and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

MARKING SCHEME
====

1. B — A person, place, thing, or idea

2. A — went

3. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Conversational Skills: Polite Language.

4. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 2.4.1 Intensive Reading: Class Reader.

5. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns.

6. A — run

7. B — Where is the library?

8. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Presentations: Oral Narratives.

9. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading: Independent Reading.

10. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns.

11. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 2.2.1 Intensive reading: Simple poems.

12. D — One main idea with supporting sentences

13. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Listening and Speaking 15.1.1 Oral Reports; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

14. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Oral Reports; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

15. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Reading 15.2.1 Reading Fluency; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

16. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Grammar in Use 15.3.1 Affirmative and Negative Sentences; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
